summary:
Wales stands under the United Kingdom's post-April 2025 regime, which now operates through statutory and quasi-statutory machinery rather than executive decree. In August 2026 the Equality and Human Rights Commission's code on single-sex spaces came into force, giving organisations compliance examples for restricting toilets, changing rooms and similar facilities to one sex. A trans visitor in Wales uses facilities designated by biological sex, and organisations are instructed on how lawfully to enforce that division.

Prison placement follows the same rule across the United Kingdom. On 19 June 2026, in For Women Scotland v Scottish Ministers [2026] CSOH 59, Lady Ross of the Outer House, Court of Session, struck down the Scottish Prison Service's non-statutory trans-custody guidance as unlawful, holding that sex segregation in prisons must rest on a lawful basis. The Welsh Prison Service operates under the same national expectation that custody segregation rest on sex.

The Welsh Government's own LGBTQ+ Action Plan for Wales, announced by Deputy Minister Hannah Blythyn in the Senedd on 21 June 2022 and published in February 2023, set the objective of making Wales the most LGBTQ+ friendly nation in Europe. It was built on 61 recommendations from the Independent LGBTQ+ Expert Panel of March 2021 and a 12-week consultation drawing 1,328 responses, and it funds a Grassroots Pride Fund. The plan records the UK Government's blocking of the Gender Recognition Reform (Scotland) Bill in January 2023.

The action plan's machinery has been maintained and updated. A version for young people was posted in January 2026, and its update page answers the For Women Scotland judgment of 19 December 2025, the date of the UK Supreme Court ruling on the definition of sex in the Equality Act 2010. The Welsh Government separately pursued a Wales-specific ban on conversion practices, forming a Working Group on Banning Conversion Practices in December 2022 and publishing 'Banning conversion practices in Wales' in May 2024.

Schools in Wales carry statutory guidance. 'Rights, Respect, Equality', out for consultation in May 2025, obliges schools to challenge bullying and harassment on grounds of sex, gender reassignment and sexual orientation, to record and monitor incidents, and to provide a parental escalation route. Transgender pupils are therefore covered by anti-bullying duties in Welsh schools while the national Equality Act 2010 protections for transgender youth remain in force.

Legal gender recognition has been available in Wales since 2004 under the Gender Recognition Act, and discrimination protections cover gender identity as well as sexual orientation. Civil partnership rights date from 2005, same-sex marriage from 2014, and full adoption rights from 2005. Same-sex sexual activity was legalised in 1967, the age of consent was equalised in 2001 and remaining restrictions removed in 2003.

Healthcare access has a distinct Welsh history. Trans adults in Wales were referred to London clinics for transgender healthcare until the first Welsh gender identity clinic opened in September 2019. In March 2024 Welsh NHS commissioners stated they had no plans to develop a children's gender service, and parents of transgender children publicly called for more help that month. Minors across the United Kingdom cannot obtain puberty blockers from NHS gender clinics under the suspension first announced by NHS England in March 2024, renewed indefinitely in December 2024 and due for reconsideration in 2027.
tangentialFactors:
The contested terrain around the Welsh programme is national. On 18 August 2026 UN human rights experts warned that UK revisions to the Equality Act 2010 risk discriminating against and excluding transgender people, and Northern Ireland, which sits on different equality legislation, was still assessing the impact of the Supreme Court ruling at that point.

Gender recognition documents carry entry consequences for visitors. In December 2023 the UK government said it would no longer accept gender recognition certificates issued by 50 countries and U.S. states, including Sweden, New York State and Belgium, on the ground that those jurisdictions allowed people to transition too easily; people from those locations must apply for a new certificate under British law to change their gender in the UK.

Scotland provides the nearest comparison for litigation over the same regime. The Court of Session heard on 5 February 2026 that housing trans prisoners by sex at birth would breach human rights and create an unacceptable suicide risk, while government lawyers defended individual risk assessments as a flexible safeguard. The 19 June 2026 judgment went the other way.

Wales' conversion-practice work mirrors a wider UK debate: the Welsh Government formed its own working group in December 2022 while the UK-wide position remained unresolved. Sport and school admissions policies set nationally also bind Welsh institutions, including the Girls' Day School Trust's January 2022 bar on trans girls without a gender recognition certificate and the July 2022 RFU and RFL single-sex policy excluding trans girls from girls' teams at under-12 level.
localsOnly:
The LGBTQ+ Action Plan for Wales is a resident-facing programme with a standing budget line, including the Grassroots Pride Fund that supports community organisations inside Wales, and a published update page that residents can consult for the Welsh Government's reading of the December 2025 Supreme Court judgment.

'Rights, Respect, Equality' gives parents in Welsh schools a defined escalation route: incidents of bullying on sex, gender reassignment or sexual orientation grounds must be recorded and monitored, and a parent can press the school through that process.

Resident healthcare runs through Welsh NHS commissioners, who in March 2024 said they had no plans to develop a children's gender service; adult services began domestically only with the first Welsh gender identity clinic in September 2019, before which referrals went to London clinics.

Legislative work on conversion practices is devolved: the Welsh Government formed a Working Group on Banning Conversion Practices in December 2022 and published 'Banning conversion practices in Wales' in May 2024, so residents are subject to whatever ban the Senedd enacts rather than a UK-wide statute.

Legal gender recognition for residents runs through the UK Gender Recognition Act in force since 2004, and a certificate will not be issued unless a spouse consents; absent that consent the marriage must be terminated.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory does not resolve whether any Welsh court or the Welsh Prison Service has itself litigated or reissued trans-custody guidance following the 19 June 2026 Scottish decision; the custody material available is Scottish.

Whether the Welsh Government's promised ban on conversion practices has been enacted, and in what form, is not established by these sources; the latest item cited is the May 2024 policy paper and the December 2022 working group.

The source set does not state whether Welsh schools have changed admissions or uniform, toilet or changing arrangements for trans pupils after the August 2026 single-sex spaces code; the school material covers anti-bullying duties only.

Open question: whether any separate Welsh statutory instrument or code modifies the Equality and Human Rights Commission's August 2026 code for devolved services such as health and social care in Wales is not sourced here.

Some background on the action plan's origins and the history of decriminalisation rests on encyclopaedic and broadcaster summaries rather than primary Welsh Government publications.
